### How to cast a “malicious” vote for `22.242.75.136`

**Endpoint**

```
POST https://www.virustotal.com/api/v2/ipaddresses/22.242.75.136/vote
```

> **Note:** If you’re using the newer v3 API, replace `/api/v2` with `/api/v3`.

**Headers**

| Header                | Value                                 |
|-----------------------|----------------------------------------|
| `X-VT-KEY`            | `<YOUR_KEY_FOUR>`                      |
| `Content-Type`        | `application/json`                     |

*(If you’re using the older V2 API, the auth header might be `x-apikey`. Check the docs.)*

**Body**

```json
{
    "type": "vote",
    "attributes": {
        "verdict": "malicious"
    }
}
```

**Example curl command**

```bash
curl -s \
     --request POST \
     --url https://www.virustotal.com/api/v2/ipaddresses/22.242.75.136/vote \
     --header "X-VT-KEY: YOUR_KEY_FOUR" \
     --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
     --data '{"type":"vote","attributes":{"verdict":"malicious"}}'
```

Replace `YOUR_KEY_FOUR` with the actual value of your `key_four`.

When you hit that URL with those headers/body, VT will record your vote against the IP. You’ll receive a response like:

```json
{
   "id":"<some-id>",
   "type":"vote",
   "links":{
      ...
   },
   "attributes":{
      "verdict":"malicious",
      "timestamp":"..."
   }
}
```

That’s all you need—just fire off the HTTP request from wherever you prefer (Postman, a script, terminal). Let me know if you’d like help wrapping this into code snippets for Python, JavaScript, etc.!
